guilds.name: Flavor Guild
guilds.description: The Flavor Guild trains cooks to understand ingredient synergy, taste balance, and sensory harmony. Members learn to build dishes where every element amplifies the whole.
guilds.philosophy: Flavor is not accident — it is architecture. Every great dish is a conversation between ingredients.
lessons: The Five Tastes: Salt, Sweet, Sour, Bitter, Umami
Acid Balance and Brightness
Fat as a Flavor Carrier
Heat and Capsaicin Dynamics
Aromatic Layering
Texture as a Flavor Element
Seasonal Ingredient Flavor Peaks
Building a Flavor Profile from Scratch

seasonal_quests.quest: Build three dishes using only spring aromatics — ramps, asparagus, peas, and fresh herbs.
Create a dish where acid is the hero: citrus, vinegar, and fermented elements.
Master the umami layer: mushrooms, aged cheese, cured meats, and miso.
Warm spice workshop: build a savory and a sweet dish using cinnamon, clove, star anise, and cardamom.

guilds.name: Sauce Guild
guilds.tagline: Where sauces become the soul of the dish
guilds.description: The Sauce Guild masters the classical French mother sauces, their derivatives, and modern interpretations. From beurre blanc to mole, members learn that a great sauce transforms everything.
guilds.philosophy: A sauce is not a condiment. It is the bridge between the cook and the diner.
lessons: The Five Mother Sauces: Béchamel, Velouté, Espagnole, Hollandaise, Tomato
Building a Fond and Deglazing
Emulsification: Stable and Broken
Reduction Technique and Nappe
Pan Sauce Fundamentals
Modern Sauces: Foams, Oils, and Vinaigrettes
Global Sauces: Mole, Chermoula, Romesco, Chimichurri
Sauce Rescue and Troubleshooting

seasonal_quests.quest: Build a hollandaise and two derivatives: béarnaise and paloise.
Create three cold sauces from scratch: aioli, salsa verde, and a fruit coulis.
Master the espagnole: build a full demi-glace from bones.
Cream sauce exploration: béchamel family with three classical derivatives.

guilds.name: Fire Guild
guilds.description: The Fire Guild trains cooks in every form of applied heat — the Maillard reaction, smoke, braising, roasting, and live-fire cooking. Heat is the cook's primary tool.
guilds.philosophy: Fire is not your enemy. It is your medium. Master heat and you master cooking.
lessons: The Maillard Reaction: Science of Browning
Pan Searing: Temperature, Protein, and Timing
Roasting: Dry Heat and Convection
Braising and Slow Cooking
Grilling: Direct vs Indirect Heat
Smoking: Wood Selection and Temperature Control
Deep Frying: Oil Temperature and Crust Development
Sous Vide and Precision Temperature Cooking
signature_techniques: The proper sear: dry protein, screaming-hot pan, no moving

seasonal_quests.quest: Grill three proteins perfectly using two-zone method: chicken, fish, and vegetable.
Live-fire week: build a full meal over open flame or charcoal only.
Braise mastery: short rib, lamb shank, and chicken thigh, three different liquid bases.
Low-and-slow smoke: brisket or pork shoulder over 8+ hours.

guilds.name: Spice Guild
guilds.tagline: Origin, aroma, and the alchemy of seasoning
guilds.description: The Spice Guild is a deep study of spice origins, aromatic chemistry, blend construction, and regional spice traditions. Members learn to season with intention and cultural awareness.
guilds.philosophy: Every spice carries a story. When you use it, you carry that story into your dish.
lessons: Spice Origins and Trade History
Toasting and Blooming Techniques
Whole vs Ground: When to Use Each
Building a Spice Blend from Scratch
The Four Spice Families: Warm, Pungent, Herbaceous, Citrus
Regional Blend Profiles: Garam Masala, Ras el Hanout, Za'atar, Berbere
Salt as a Spice Carrier
Balancing Heat, Warmth, and Aroma

seasonal_quests.quest: Create three herbaceous blends using spring-fresh herbs and light spices.
Build a regional rub: North African, Jamaican jerk, or Indian tikka masala blend.
Warm spice deep dive: cinnamon, allspice, clove, nutmeg in savory applications.
Spice extraction: make three infused oils, tinctures, or aromatic sugars.

guilds.name: Heritage Guild
guilds.tagline: Cook with roots, cook with respect
guilds.description: The Heritage Guild is the cultural heart of The Culinary Guild. Members explore Cajun, Creole, Gullah Geechee, Native American, and global food traditions with historical depth and culinary respect.
guilds.philosophy: Tradition is not a limitation. It is a living archive of human ingenuity and survival.
lessons: Cajun Cuisine: Bayou to Table
Creole Cooking: The Melting Pot of New Orleans
Gullah Geechee: Lowcountry Food Traditions
Native American Foodways: Three Sisters and Beyond
West African Culinary Roots
The African Diaspora in American Cooking
Mediterranean Food Philosophy
Southeast Asian Flavor Systems
signature_techniques: The Cajun trinity (onion, celery, bell pepper)

seasonal_quests.quest: Cook a full Gullah Geechee spring table: red rice, oysters, and spring greens.
West African summer feast: jollof rice, suya, and a cold hibiscus drink.
Native American harvest: Three Sisters stew, fry bread, and roasted game.
New Orleans winter soul: gumbo, red beans and rice, and beignets.

guilds.name: Bake Guild
guilds.tagline: Precision is the ingredient you cannot taste
guilds.description: The Bake Guild teaches precision baking, pastry fundamentals, and the science of rise, crumb, and crust. From sourdough to celebration cakes, baking is chemistry with a delicious result.
guilds.philosophy: Baking rewards patience and precision. Measure twice, taste once.
lessons: The Science of Gluten Development
Leavening: Yeast, Baking Soda, and Baking Powder
Mixing Methods: Creaming, Reverse Creaming, All-in-One
Cake Structure and Crumb Science
Pastry Doughs: Pâte Brisée, Sucrée, and Feuilletée
Bread Fundamentals: Hydration, Fermentation, and Shaping
Chocolate Tempering and Ganache
Scaling Recipes: The Rose Factor Method

seasonal_quests.quest: Spring pastry collection: lemon tart, strawberry chiffon cake, and a seasonal galette.
Cold baking challenge: ice cream cake, semifreddo, and no-bake cheesecake.
Spiced bake week: apple tarte tatin, pumpkin bread, and a chai pound cake.
Celebration baking: build a layered layer cake with buttercream and a yule log.

guilds.name: Broth Hall
guilds.tagline: Everything begins with a great stock
guilds.description: The Broth Hall is dedicated to stocks, broths, soups, and stews — the foundation of classical cooking. Members learn that depth, body, and flavor all start in the pot.
guilds.philosophy: A cook who understands stock understands cooking.
lessons: Stock Fundamentals: Bones, Water, Aromatics, Time
White Stock vs Brown Stock
Consommé: The Art of Clarification
Cream Soups: Bisques and Velouté-Based Soups
Chowders: Dairy, Tomato, and Clear Styles
Ramen Broth Deep Dive: Tonkotsu, Shio, Shoyu, Miso
Global Soup Traditions: Pho, Caldo, Borscht, Harira
Texture and Garnish: Finishing the Bowl
signature_techniques: Cold water start for clear stock
Finishing with fresh herbs and acid

seasonal_quests.quest: Light spring broth: asparagus velouté and a clear spring vegetable consommé.
Cold soup collection: gazpacho, vichyssoise, and a chilled fruit soup.
Roasted bone broth: make a 12-hour beef bone broth and a French onion soup.
Ramen deep dive: build a tonkotsu or miso ramen from scratch including tare.

guilds.name: Mixology Chamber
guilds.tagline: Balance, build, and shake with purpose
guilds.description: The Mixology Chamber covers cocktail theory, spirit profiles, technique, and food pairing. Members learn that great drinks follow the same principles as great food — balance, acid, sugar, and dilution.
guilds.philosophy: A cocktail is a meal in a glass. Treat it with the same care.
lessons: The Six Classic Cocktail Families: Sour, Old Fashioned, Highball, Flip, Fizz, Punch
Spirit Profiles: Whiskey, Rum, Gin, Tequila, Vodka, Brandy
The Golden Ratio: Spirit, Sweet, Sour
Bitters: Function and Application
Ice Theory: Dilution, Temperature, and Texture
Infusions and Fat-Washing
Food and Drink Pairing Principles
Classic Cocktail History from Jerry Thomas to Today
signature_techniques: Shaking vs stirring (and why it matters)

seasonal_quests.quest: Spring floral cocktails: elderflower, lavender, and fresh herb syrups.
Frozen and sparkling: build three fizzes and a frozen daiquiri variation.
Warm and stirred: build an old fashioned family — classic, mezcal, and rum.
Holiday punch bowl: build a batched punch for 8 using spirit, citrus, and spice.

guilds.name: Otaku Culinary Guild
guilds.tagline: Cook the meals that made you want to live inside the story
guilds.description: The Otaku Culinary Guild is where anime-inspired cooking meets serious culinary craft. Members recreate iconic anime-inspired dishes, explore fantasy tavern menus, and compete in fandom-themed kitchen trials.
guilds.philosophy: Food in anime is not decoration — it is emotion. When you recreate it, you carry that feeling into the real world.
lessons: Japanese Comfort Food: Rice, Miso, and Umami
Ramen from Scratch: Broth, Tare, Noodles, and Toppings
Bento Box Design: Balance, Color, and Nutrition
Anime Tavern Foods: Stews, Roasts, and Bread
Festival Street Foods: Takoyaki, Taiyaki, Yakitori
Yoshoku: Western-Japanese Fusion Cooking
Fantasy Cuisine: Mapping Fictional Dishes to Real Recipes
Omurice and Katsu Curry: Crowd Favorites Done Right

seasonal_quests.quest: Spring bento challenge: create a full bento with spring colors, cherry blossom themes, and balanced nutrition.
Anime summer festival: recreate three classic summer matsuri foods.
Isekai tavern week: build a fantasy tavern menu with stew, roast, and hearty bread.
Winter arc comfort: create a warming anime-inspired ramen bowl and a sweet companion dessert.
